text: {"decisions":[{"candidate_id":"E13","decision":"revise","major_issues":["The normalized comparison still leaves major uncontrolled donor-linked properties entangled because matching MeCN/H2O and total amine-derived fraction does not match proton activity, CO2 uptake/speciation, viscosity, conductivity, or cobalt coordination between TEA and TEOA.","The card lacks an internal no-amine or non-CO2 control within the specified groups, so apparent donor-dependent gas differences rely on external workflow checks rather than built-in attribution controls.","The stated inference can overread collapse of the TEA/TEOA difference as mainly medium/proton-management causation, when normalization itself changes several hidden variables and may differentially affect catalyst viability."],"rationale":"This is a useful within-platform comparison anchored by direct system evidence for the P01 formulation family and by transferable evidence that amines and medium can alter CO2-reduction behavior. It has clear value as a descriptive test of whether a TEA/TEOA difference survives tighter recipe matching. However, the proposed primary contrast does not isolate donor identity versus medium effects as strongly as claimed, because TEA and TEOA remain chemically non-equivalent even at matched volume fraction and solvent ratio. Current assessment acknowledges the card's own cautions about bulk-versus-local mismatch, but newly identifies the uptake proxy and correlation-to-causation leap as unresolved issues requiring revision."}],"overall":"E15 and E17 are the strongest candidates for shortlist because they ask bounded questions with interpretations that remain aligned to the actual controls.
